name: Beken SPI LED Strip
description: This is a component using the Beken SPI DMA interface to drive addressable LED strips.

config_entries.label: Name
config_entries.description: The name of the light. At least one of **id** and **name** must be specified.

config_entries.label: Icon
config_entries.description: Manually set the icon to use for the light in the frontend.

config_entries.label: Pin
config_entries.description: The pin for the data line of the light.

config_entries.label: Restore Mode
config_entries.description: Control how the light attempts to restore state on bootup. Mutually exclusive with `restore_state`. > [!WARNING] > `restore_mode` is deprecated in favor of `restore_state` (above), which offers the same behavior plus > per-field control. `restore_mode` is not currently scheduled for removal and all 8 values below continue > to work as described.

options.label: RESTORE_DEFAULT_OFF
options.description: Attempt to restore state and default to OFF if not possible to restore.

options.label: RESTORE_DEFAULT_ON
options.description: Attempt to restore state and default to ON.

options.label: ALWAYS_OFF
options.description: Always initialize the light as OFF on bootup.

options.label: ALWAYS_ON
options.description: Always initialize the light as ON on bootup.

options.label: RESTORE_INVERTED_DEFAULT_OFF
options.description: Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to OFF.

options.label: RESTORE_INVERTED_DEFAULT_ON
options.description: Attempt to restore state inverted from the previous state and default to ON.

options.label: RESTORE_AND_OFF
options.description: Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as OFF.

options.label: RESTORE_AND_ON
options.description: Attempt to restore state but initialize the light as ON.

config_entries.label: Channel Colors
config_entries.description: The order in which the strip expects its color channels. List each of `R`, `G` and `B` exactly once, optionally with a single `W` in any position; for example `GRB`, `BGR`, `GRBW`, `WRGB` or `RWGB`. The value is case-insensitive. Including a `W` makes this a four channel RGBW strip.

config_entries.label: Chipset
config_entries.description: The chipset to apply known timings from.

config_entries.label: Num Leds
config_entries.description: The number of LEDs in the strip. The DMA buffer limits this to 165 LEDs, or 123 LEDs when `channel_colors` contains a `W`.

config_entries.label: Disabled By Default
config_entries.description: If true, then this entity should not be added to any client's frontend, (usually Home Assistant) without the user manually enabling it (via the Home Assistant UI). Defaults to `false`.

config_entries.label: Effects
config_entries.description: A list of [light effects](https://esphome.io/components/light#light-effects) to use for this light.

config_entries.label: Entity Category
config_entries.description: The category of the entity. See [this list](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/#generic-properties) for a list of available options. Set to `""` to remove the default entity category.

config_entries.label: Initial State
config_entries.description: The initial state the light should be set to on bootup, applied before any state is restored via `restore_mode` or `restore_state` (below). If restoring is configured and a previous state is successfully loaded, the loaded (and, for `restore_state`, possibly overridden) values take precedence over **initial_state** for the fields they touch. If neither `restore_mode` nor `restore_state` is set, **initial_state**'s `state` is honored as-is on every boot. If `restore_mode` **is** set, its own cold-boot direction (`OFF` for `RESTORE_DEFAULT_OFF`, `RESTORE_INVERTED_DEFAULT_OFF`, `RESTORE_AND_OFF` and `ALWAYS_OFF`; `ON` for the other four values) always overrides **initial_state**'s `state`. > [!WARNING] > Before 2026.10.0, a light whose `initial_state` set `state: ON` and had neither `restore_mode` nor `restore_state` > set would still boot OFF, because omitting both keys implicitly behaved like `restore_mode: ALWAYS_OFF`. > This was counter-intuitive and has been fixed: such a light now boots ON, as `initial_state` says.

config_entries.label: Blue
config_entries.description: The blue channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Brightness
config_entries.description: The primary brightness of the light; applies to all channels (both color and white) of the light.

config_entries.label: Cold White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the cold white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: Color
config_entries.description: A [standard CSS color name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/named-color), for example `red` or `springgreen`, or a hex value in the form `0xRRGGBB`, for example `0x223344`, used instead of **red**, **green** and **blue**. Names are not case-sensitive. Cannot be used together with **red**, **green** or **blue**. This option is not templatable. The light always drives its brightest color channel at full level. For a dark color such as `darkred` or `0x223344`, the **color_brightness** is therefore set to match (about 55% and 27% respectively). Colors with a channel at full level, such as `red`, set **color_brightness** to 100%. If you also set **color_brightness**, your value is used instead, and a warning is logged if the color is a dark one. Color names such as `white` and `gray` are converted to RGB colors only and do not affect the white channel, if present.

config_entries.label: Color Brightness
config_entries.description: The brightness of the color lights. Useful to control brightness of colored and white lights separately for RGBW lights.

config_entries.label: Color Mode
config_entries.description: For lights that support more than one color mode, the color mode that will be activated. The color mode determines which outputs of the light are active, and which parameters can be used. For example, this can be used to switch between colored and white light. Must be a color mode that is supported by the light. Valid color modes are:

config_entries.label: Color Temperature
config_entries.description: The color temperature (in [mireds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mired) or Kelvin) of the white channel.

config_entries.label: Green
config_entries.description: The green channel of the light.

config_entries.label: Red
config_entries.description: The red channel of the light.

config_entries.label: State
config_entries.description: The ON/OFF state for the light.

config_entries.label: Warm White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the warm white channel. Cannot be used at the same time as *color_temperature*.

config_entries.label: White
config_entries.description: The brightness of the white channel.

config_entries.label: Internal
config_entries.description: Mark this component as internal. Internal components will not be exposed to the frontend (like Home Assistant). Only specifying an `id` without a `name` will implicitly set this to true.

config_entries.label: Max Refresh Rate
config_entries.description: A time interval used to limit the number of commands a light can handle per second. For example 16ms will limit the light to a refresh rate of about 60Hz. Defaults to sending commands as quickly as changes are made to the lights.

config_entries.label: Restore State
config_entries.description: Persist the light's state to flash and restore it on bootup, with optional per-field overrides applied on top of whatever was loaded. Mutually exclusive with `restore_mode`. Accepts a mapping of per-field overrides, or one of two case-insensitive shorthands: `all` or `none`. If nothing has been saved yet (e.g. on the very first boot), restoring has nothing to do, so the light falls back to **initial_state** (or its hardware defaults) instead — none of the fields below take effect until a state has actually been persisted at least once.

config_entries.label: State
config_entries.description: `KEEP` (default, case-insensitive) to restore the saved ON/OFF state as-is, `INVERT` to restore it inverted, `INITIAL` to use **initial_state**'s state instead (OFF if **initial_state** doesn't set one), or an explicit `ON`/`OFF` (or boolean) to always force this value regardless of what was saved.

config_entries.label: Resume Effect
config_entries.description: Remember the effect that was running when the light was turned off, and start it again when the light is next turned on with a plain turn-on. A turn-on that also sets an effect, brightness, color or transition uses those instead. The remembered effect is kept in memory only, so it is lost on reboot. Defaults to `false`.
